title: Client Semver Adapter and Deprecation Timeline for Legacy Inference Endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We will provide a small, short-lived 'semver adapter' on the platform and SDKs to help client libraries transition from legacy inference endpoints to the unified /v2 inference API. The adapter surfaces a compatibility layer that maps legacy request fields and model aliases to the new spec, while emitting enriched telemetry to gate deprecation. This ticket captures the PRD-level requirements, scope, rollout phases, acceptance criteria, and migration timelines. Motivation: Many customers rely on older SDK versions or on model aliases that differ between v1 and v2. A temporary adapter reduces customer breakage while allowing us to enforce the new API shape and accelerate decommissioning of the legacy routing layer. Goals: - Provide a one-release-lifetime semver adapter for Redwood-hosted endpoints and SDKs that: 1) reliably translates legacy requests to v2, 2) emits migration telemetry, 3) supports opt-in telemetry-tagged shadowing for canary customers. - Define a 3-phase deprecation timeline with clear gates (telemetry, compatibility tests, SDK adoption rates). - Surface deterministic rollback and cutover criteria to SRE and Support. Out of scope: - On‑prem/private deployments (handled by Private roadmap). - Automatic model retraining or output normalization. - Building permanent long-term compatibility shims in dedicated deployments. Key stakeholders: - Product (owner: Aisha Patel) - Engineering (serving runtime: Diego Rivera; SDKs: Priya Nandakumar) - Developer Experience (docs: Joshua Kim) - SRE/Infra (lead: Carla Gomez) - Support/CS (lead: Maya Singh)
technical_requirements: Adapter must accept legacy endpoint paths and HTTP payload shapes and translate to /v2/generate or /v2/chat as appropriate
Adapter must preserve request-level headers used for authentication and routing (Authorization, Redwood-Client-Version, X-Region) without content loss
Adapter must map legacy model aliases to canonical v2 model aliases using the onboarded model catalog; provide a fallback policy when alias is unmapped
Adapter should flag requests that rely on deprecated parameters (e.g., n_best, stop_sequence[]) and convert where deterministic; otherwise surface a clear client error with migration guidance
Emit telemetry events for each adapted request including fields: legacy_endpoint, mapped_model, mapping_status (mapped|fallback|missing), client_version, and adapter_version
Add a feature-flagged 'shadow_mode' that duplicates incoming requests to both legacy code path and the v2 path for metrics comparison without impacting response latency
SDKs (Python/Node/Go) must include a single-line opt-in toggle to enable adapter compatibility for pre-2.0 clients
Adapter must support a configurable sampling rate for telemetry (default 100% for first 4 weeks, then adjustable by product/SRE)
Performance SLA: adapter should add no more than 35 ms median additional latency at p50 and 100 ms at p95 under normal traffic profiles
Adapter must honor customer tenant isolation and never persist plaintext prompt content to third-party stores; logging must comply with PII redaction rules
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design & Readout): 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-21 — finalize mapping table, UX copy for SDKs/docs, and telemetry schema

Phase 1 (Alpha Canary): 2026-02-22 to 2026-03-14 — deploy adapter behind feature flag for internal and select enterprise canaries; enable 100% telemetry sampling; collect mapping failure rates and latency deltas
Phase 2 (Public Opt-In): 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-11 — enable SDK opt-in toggles and document migration guide; open adapter to opt-in customers and surface self-service compatibility report in Console

Phase 3 (Mandatory Warning Window): 2026-04-12 to 2026-04-25 — responses include deprecation-warning header and telemetry to measure active legacy usage; begin scheduled outbound customer notifications
Phase 4 (Read-Only Protective Mode): 2026-04-26 to 2026-04-30 — limit new legacy requests to lower qps and show explicit 429+Retry-After for clients hitting quota; offer migration assistant support

Phase 5 (Cutover & Shutdown): 2026-05-01 — adapter removed from public routing; legacy endpoint DNS/routes shut down for hosted API. Private/Dedicated customers will receive a separate migration window.
acceptance_criteria: Mapping table covers >98% of historical alias mappings for top 300 customer models (verified by query against model-catalog exports)
Adapter telemetry pipeline ingests events reliably with <0.1% loss and metrics visible on Console dashboard
Median latency overhead for adapter under synthetic load tests is <=35 ms and p95 <=100 ms

All SDKs publish a new release (minor version) that includes adapter opt-in flag, migration messages, and automated tests; each SDK repo has at least one integration test validating request translation
Support playbook and migration FAQ published in Confluence with migration commands, common failure cases, and contact routing
No customer-facing P0 incidents attributable to adapter behavior during Alpha Canary phase
Telemetry thresholds defined: if mapping_failure_rate >2% for two consecutive days, pause public rollout and create ENG follow-up ticket
Rollout gate: >=60% of active clients sending legacy requests must either have adapter opt-in or be scheduled for assisted migration before Mandatory Warning Window
docs_and_comms: SDK changelog entries and migration snippets included in python/node/go release notes
Customer announcement cadence: email (T-30 days), In-console banner (T-21 days), Webinar office hours (T-14 days), Direct outreach for top 50 customers (T-10 days)
telemetry_gates_and_metrics: Traffic adoption rate: percent of legacy requests routed through adapter opt-in vs. direct legacy path
SDK adoption: percent of active client tokens reporting adapter_version >= 1.0
Support volume: new migration-related tickets per day (target <50/day during Public Opt-In)
Shadow output drift metric when shadow_mode enabled: mismatch_rate threshold 1% for top-5 intents
rollback_criteria: If adapter causes customer-impacting errors (>0.5% total error increase sustained for 4 hours), disable adapter and revert routing
If adapter telemetry pipeline shows >1% event loss for 24 hours, pause rollout and fail safe to legacy routing
If p95 latency delta breaches 200 ms repeatedly for 2 hours, automatically disable adapter feature flag and alert SRE
All rollbacks must trigger postmortem and follow-up remediation story assigned within 48 hours
